comments.note: Port is cast from int to uint for MySqlConnectionStringBuilder. The guard `active.Port > 0 ? active.Port : 3306` silently replaces 0 with the MySQL default. If port 0 is a deliberate sentinel (e.g. 'not set'), callers could be surprised. A validation step in DatabaseConnectionOptions or a Guard.Against.NonPositive at the DI boundary would make the contract explicit.

SslMode is mapped to Required vs. Disabled with no in-between option (e.g. Preferred). This is intentional for clarity; future callers wanting Preferred would need an enum expansion on DatabaseConnectionOptions.

comments.note: If MySqlConnection.OpenAsync throws (e.g., connection refused), the created MySqlConnection instance is not disposed before the exception propagates. This is a minor resource management gap — the connection will be finalized by GC. Not an AC concern since factory callers own the lifetime of the returned connection, but a future refactor could wrap the open in try/finally to dispose on failure.

Port=0 fallback to 3306 carries forward from the Developer's implementation note. Explicit validation in DatabaseConnectionOptions or at the DI boundary would make the contract clearer. Non-blocking for this WP.

summary: Reviewed 1 primary artifact (MySqlConnectionFactory.cs) plus supporting context (DatabaseConnectionOptions.cs, JsonDatabaseConnectionStore.cs, JsonSettingsService.cs, Sha256FixedSaltPasswordHasher.cs). Full OWASP Top 10 review completed. 0 Critical, 0 High, 2 Medium, 2 Low findings. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: A02 — Cryptographic Failures | MEDIUM | File: src/VideoIndexer.Core/Options/DatabaseConnectionOptions.cs, line 37 (Password property). MySQL connection passwords are persisted as plaintext strings in the JSON settings file. The field docstring explicitly acknowledges this: 'Login password (plaintext; stored at the user's discretion).' Because the password must be recoverable to authenticate to MySQL, hashing/KDF is not viable. However, the credential is unprotected at rest — any process running as the same OS user (or with file-read access to the settings path) can recover it in cleartext. Remediation: Encrypt credentials at rest using Windows DPAPI (System.Security.Cryptography.ProtectedData.Protect) keyed to the current user, or store in Windows Credential Manager via Windows.Security.Credentials.PasswordVault. Decrypt only at the moment CreateOpenConnectionAsync is called.

A02/A04 — Cryptographic Failures / Insecure Design | MEDIUM | File: src/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure/Database/MySqlConnectionFactory.cs, line 43. SslMode is set to MySqlSslMode.Disabled when UseSsl = false (the default value). A user connecting to a remote MySQL server over an untrusted network without enabling SSL will transmit credentials and query data in cleartext. The binary choice (Required vs. Disabled) also skips MySqlSslMode.Preferred, which would negotiate encryption when the server supports it without failing on servers that don't. Remediation: Change the ternary to: active.UseSsl ? MySqlSslMode.Required : MySqlSslMode.Preferred. Reserve Disabled for an explicit third enum value (e.g., SslPolicy.ForceOff) to prevent accidental unencrypted connections.

A05 — Security Misconfiguration | LOW | File: src/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure/Settings/JsonSettingsService.cs. The settings file (which contains plaintext DB credentials) is written without explicit file-permission hardening. File.WriteAllTextAsync uses the system default ACL, leaving the file readable by other processes running as the same user account and by administrators. Remediation: On Windows, after writing the file, apply a restrictive ACL via System.Security.AccessControl.FileSecurity restricting access to the current user SID only. On Linux/macOS, chmod 600 via File.SetUnixFileMode.

A09 — Security Logging & Monitoring Failures | LOW | File: src/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure/Database/MySqlConnectionFactory.cs. No ILogger is injected; connection open events and failures are not logged. If OpenAsync throws (e.g., authentication failure, connection refused), the exception propagates silently with no audit trail. Remediation: Inject ILogger<MySqlConnectionFactory> and log (at Debug level) successful opens and (at Warning/Error level) connection failures, omitting the password from log output.

summary: Code review PASS. Implementation is clean, well-structured, and meets all three acceptance criteria. One Fix-Forward applied: wrapped MySqlConnection.OpenAsync in try/catch to dispose the connection on failure, preventing a resource leak when the open fails (e.g., wrong credentials, network error). Fix is non-behavioral on the happy path; all 87 tests remain green. No Blocking issues found.

comments.note: Resource leak on OpenAsync failure (Fix-Forward applied). File: src/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure/Database/MySqlConnectionFactory.cs. If MySqlConnection.OpenAsync throws (e.g., wrong credentials, connection refused, CancellationToken triggered), the MySqlConnection instance was previously abandoned without disposal. Wrapped the open call in try/catch to call DisposeAsync() before re-throwing. This is a non-behavioral change on the success path; all 87 tests pass unchanged. Pattern: try { await connection.OpenAsync(...); return connection; } catch { await connection.DisposeAsync(); throw; }

[documentation-forward] MySqlConnectionFactory.cs passes DatabaseConnectionOptions nullable string properties (Host, Database, Username) directly to MySqlConnectionStringBuilder without null guards. If a saved connection has a null Host or Database, the failure will manifest as a MySqlConnector exception rather than an application-level ArgumentException. Document in the factory XML doc or in DatabaseConnectionOptions that callers/persistence layer must ensure these fields are non-null before a connection entry is considered valid for use.

Port guard '(uint)(active.Port > 0 ? active.Port : 3306)' is slightly redundant: DatabaseConnectionOptions.Port already defaults to 3306, so Port=0 can only occur if a caller explicitly sets it. Not blocking — the guard is a safe fallback — but if Port=0 is invalid, a validation step at the save/DI boundary would make the contract explicit (consistent with the Developer's own improvement note).
